Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The West Indies players are in a huddle and then they spread out to take their respective field positions. David Warner has a new opening partner in Mitchell Marsh. Alzarri Joseph to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Australia, on the other hand, started brilliantly with the debutant setting the tone by picking up a wicket in his very first over while Behrendorff followed it up with another. Bartlett got another in his second over, and even though they let the batters settle in, Zampa and Hardie made sure to half of the opposition back to the hut inside. However, after that, they were hit by a powerful Windies storm and just did not have any answers. They conceded 84 runs in the last five overs and Adam Zampa ended up with his most expensive T20I spell. Spencer Johnson did manage to get rid of Andre Russell in the last over but by then all the damage was done. Their batting unit has scored more than 200 runs in the last two games, but now they will have to do with the pressure of the asking rate. This will probably be the last T20I innings for David Warner in Australia and he will want to lead the charge for the Aussies. It is going to be an exciting run chase. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Andre Russell, one of the architects of the Windies innings is up for a chat. He says that he is happy to entertain the crowd and contribute to the team. Adds that they were 5 wickets down but wasn't going to panic and he knew Rutherford is a dangerous player and a few more were still to come and just went for his shots. Mentions that he knew that was the last over for Zampa and last over of spin as well, so, he decided to just take on every ball of that over. Ends by saying that the wicket is pretty good but if they bowl good lines and lengths, they can win the game.

After electing to bat first, the top order failed miserably as Johnson Charles, Nicholas Pooran, and Kyle Mayers all went back cheaply inside the Powerplay. The move to promote Roston Chase worked out well as he counter-attacked nicely along with the skipper Rovman Powell. They set up a good platform with a 55-run partnership but unfortunately were dismissed in quick succession putting them on the back foot again. Dre Russ took a nasty blow early on, but that only woke him up while Sherfane Rutherford struggled very much initially but hung around there and did not throw his wicket away. Andre Russell continued to attack from one end, but once his partner got set, he took a back seat and enjoyed the Rutherford show who notched up his maiden T20I fifty in the process as well. Russell went bang bang in the second last over and smashed Zampa for four sixes, but got out in the last over after smacking 71 off just 29 balls while Rutherford remained unbeaten on 67.

West Indies have put in a strong batting effort here! The whole crowd in the Optus Stadium is on their feet applauding Sherfane Rutherford as he walks back to the hut. It was the Russell-Rutherford show here and everyone here has been thoroughly entertained with their Caribbean flare. West Indies were struggling at 79/5, but a massive partnership of 139 runs between the dynamic duo has given the Windies a really good chance of finishing the tour on a good note.

An anti-climatic end to the innings but West Indies have done the damage in the last 5 overs or so! Spencer Johnson steams in and bowls a wide yorker, Romario Shepherd stays leg side of the ball and fails to squeeze it away. The batters decide against going for a bye and West Indies finish with 220/6 on the board!

West Indies, on the other hand, showed fight in both the games, but couldn't get over the line. The problem for them has been their bowling as they have conceded a lot of runs. Alzarri Joseph has been their standout bowler but will need more support from others. As we have seen over the years, they do have some strong power-hitters like Nicholas Pooran, Andre Russell, and skipper Rovman Powell, but the only thing missing from their game is they need to perform as a collective unit to have any chance of beating the Aussies. Will the Windies finish on a high? Or will the hosts complete the whitewash? We will find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

Australia have been absolutely brilliant in both the games especially with the bat. They have scored well over 200 in both games which also includes a sensational hundred from Glenn Maxwell in the last game. They do pose a pretty dangerous batting line up and it is difficult to get away from them as someone or the other will get you eventually. Surprisingly Marcus Stoinis have done well with the bowl while Josh Hazlewood continues to be their most consistent frontline pacer across all formats of the game.

Hello and a warm welcome folks! We are at the Optus Stadium in Burswood for the 3rd and final T20I between Australia and West Indies. This has been a good preparation for both sides with the T20 World Cup not too far away. The Aussies have already sealed the series and will be eying for the whitewash while the Windies will hope to end their tour on a positive note.
... MATCH DAY ...

West Indies tour to Australia has been a pretty long one and it has been a tour that has provided us with some fabulous memories as well in Tests and in the T20Is but the ODI series was pretty one-sided. It is now time for one last game on the tour as both teams gear up for the 3rd and final T20I to be played at the Perth Stadium in Perth. Australia have won the series 2-0 already but will be eyeing a whitewash just like in the ODI series whereas West Indies will be looking to end the tour on a high. The first two games of the T20I series saw both teams score more than 200 runs in every single innings and we witnessed some unreal hitting. The 2nd T20I in Adelaide was a remarkable one as Glenn Maxwell aka 'The Big Show' did in fact put on a big show as he scored his record-equalling fifth T20I century and played some unbelievable shots on the way too. David Warner looked good at the top once again but the thing the Aussies will be happy about would be Tim David consistently firing in the death overs, something that had gone missing in the past year or so. Spencer Johnson got a game in and the left-arm quick once again made his mark and he just continues to show that he can roll with the big boys. The hosts will look to tighten their bowling a bit as the pacers did go for plenty, especially Jason Behrendorff who isn't quite enjoying bowling at the death. West Indies on the other hand have been able to conjure up something of a comeback with the bat in the death overs but inconsistency at the top of the order and in the middle order cost them both games. The likes of Brandon King, Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford haven't been able to string two good performances in a row and most of the work has been left to the likes of skipper Rovman Powell and Andre Russell, both of whom did a fine job in the last game but they simply had a mountain to climb. The bowling has been patchy with Akeal Hosein simply not being able to weave his magic in the Powerplay but Alzarri Joseph did bowl a stellar spell in the last game and he looks like the only one who tries to improve every game and give it his all. The Windies need to bowl well as they have enough batting depth to score big but if they keep conceding well above 200 runs every time, even that muscle power won't be able to chase it down. Can West Indies end their tour Down-Under with a win? Or will Australia overpower them yet again? We shall find out.
